sections.h2: Missoula and the land under your house
sections.html:
Western Montana is home to Missoula, which lies at 3,209 feet and under 25 miles from Idaho. Its roughly 35 square miles occupy a flat valley floor, bounded by Mount Sentinel and Mount Jumbo. Housing runs from older blocks near the river up to lots cut into the hillsides.

Terrain changes the sale. A river-bottom parcel, a steep lot and a house served by the rural fire district beyond city limits each come with a different tax bill and different buyer questions, so pull up your own parcel record before listing.

Many separate bodies set rates, but you receive one bill. The County Clerk and Treasurer collects for all of them, which means county, city, school, fire, transit and state university levies can share a statement. The 2026 notice lists the six biggest ones likely to show up:

  • Missoula County Public Schools
  • City of Missoula
  • Missoula County
  • Missoula Urban Transportation District (Mountain Line)
  • Missoula Rural Fire District
  • Montana University System

Water, sewer, irrigation or bus districts can tack on more lines. Online, the county's tax lookup accepts a last name, address, geocode or taxpayer ID and charts the share each jurisdiction takes.

Missoula County wants the 2026 first-half payment postmarked on or before Monday, November 30, 2026, with the second half due Tuesday, June 1, 2027. One invoice covers both, and nothing more arrives in the mail for the second half. Mailing between November 26 and 30? Take it to the post office counter and ask a clerk to postmark it on the spot.

State law (MCA 15-16-102) uses 5 p.m. on November 30 and May 31 as the usual cutoffs, with weekends and holidays rolling forward a business day. Owners who live in the house may choose a seven-payment plan that starts November 30 and ends May 31.

Skip the bill and the county gets a claim against your house that closing must settle. The cutoff is whatever date and time your October or November bill shows. After it, a 2% penalty is added and interest builds at 10% annually, which state law expresses as 5/6 of 1% per month.

  • Late June or early July: mailed delinquency notices.
  • First business day of August: the claim is recorded, with a $75 tax lien certificate fee added.
  • Late August: an investor can buy the lien by assignment.
  • After the lien date, the county describes a two to three year period to pay before the property is at risk.

Have the title company calculate a payoff through closing day, penalty and interest included. A lien does not kill a deal. The money simply comes off the top of what you receive, and an August lien gets handled that way too.

sections.h2: The 2026 rate change and empty houses
sections.html:
Living in a house earns a better rate than owning it as a second home. For 2026 the Department of Revenue sets 0.76% on market value up to $378,000, 0.90% from there to $756,000, 1.10% from there to $1,511,999, and 1.90% on whatever is left.

All other property pays a flat 1.90%. That bucket holds second homes, short-term rentals and empty residential lots. To get the lower rate, you must occupy the house for seven or more months, or rent it long term with stays of 28 days or longer across at least seven months.

Heirs and landlords should pay attention. An inherited house nobody lives in, or a rental that goes vacant, may lose the lower rate. The department's 2026 property tax page covers enrollment and refunds.

Your value comes from the state, not the city or county, so the Department of Revenue is the first stop. It reappraises homes on a two-year cycle, and Missoula's treasurer urges owners to act the moment the notice arrives.

There are two ways in. Submit an informal classification and appraisal review request (Form AB-26) online, or go straight to the Missoula County Tax Appeal Board with the application at mtab.mt.gov/appealform. The property record card showing the buildings and features the state counted is posted online, and errors on it are worth catching before you file.

sections.h2: Paperwork when a Missoula house is sold
sections.html:
Montana requires a Realty Transfer Certificate with every deed sent to the county clerk and recorder for recording. A wrong or missing certificate can mean a $500 penalty, six months in jail, or both. The form asks for:

  • Seller and buyer names and mailing addresses, with the last four digits of each one's Social Security or federal ID number.
  • Whether it was your principal residence, which means you occupied it at least seven months.
  • Price, plus whether financing was cash, FHA, VA or contract.
  • Your signature on a water right disclosure.

Gain on the sale counts as Montana-source income and belongs on your return, and the state matches ID numbers against income tax filings. On city water, tick the public-supply box. Questions about water rights go to the Missoula office of the Department of Natural Resources and Conservation, which serves Granite, Mineral, Missoula and Ravalli counties.

A tidy sale tends to run in this sequence. First, look up your bill through the county's online tool and note whether the first half has been paid. Second, check the property record card and the rate class your house was taxed under. Third, ask the title company for a payoff statement that runs to the closing date. Fourth, gather the details the Realty Transfer Certificate asks for, so the deed and certificate reach the clerk and recorder together. Fifth, if you also hold a mortgage, request its payoff in writing so you can see what is left after tax and closing costs.

sections.h2: When the house needs a roof or furnace
sections.html: Cold, moderately snowy winters and hot, dry summers wear on roofs, gutters, furnaces and exterior paint, and inspectors check every one. A tired roof or furnace can derail a listing at the inspection stage. A cash buyer who takes the place as is skips that negotiation, though the offer will account for the condition.

faqs.q: What is Missoula property tax and who collects it?
faqs.a: It is a set of levies from the county, city, schools, fire, transit and the university system, all collected by the Missoula County Clerk and Treasurer. The Montana Department of Revenue sets the value, and the county bills it.

faqs.q: When is Missoula property tax due?
faqs.a: The first half of the 2026 bill must be postmarked by Monday, November 30, 2026, and the second half is due Tuesday, June 1, 2027. A deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Missoula house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax, penalty and interest are paid from your proceeds at closing, so the title company needs a current payoff amount. A lien that attached in August can be cleared the same way.

faqs.q: What form do I file when I sell a house in Missoula?
faqs.a: A Realty Transfer Certificate, filed with the Missoula County Clerk and Recorder when the deed is recorded. It covers parties, price, financing, principal residence status and water rights.

faqs.q: Does an empty inherited house in Missoula get the lower tax rate?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The tiered rate is for primary residences and qualifying long-term rentals, and second homes and vacant residential lots pay a flat 1.90%.
